objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with a chronic cough, difficulty walking up stairs which improves after exercise, and significant weight loss.

turns.content: Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—first, how long has your chronic cough lasted, and is it dry or producing phlegm/blood? Patient: Doctor: Do you get shortness of breath or chest pain, and have you noticed fevers or night sweats? Patient: Doctor: About the walking issue: when you climb stairs, do your legs feel weak/painful/short of breath, and does it improve after you keep going?

Patient: My cough has been going on for about three months, and it’s mostly dry—no blood and no fevers or night sweats. When I climb stairs my legs feel weak and slow, but if I keep moving and warm up, it actually improves somewhat.

Doctor: Thanks—any wheezing/itchy throat, reflux/heartburn, or smoking/exposure to TB/chemicals? Also, have you lost weight without trying, and do you get numbness/tingling or any swelling/pain in your legs?

Patient: I do smoke about a pack a day for 35 years, but I don’t recall wheezing or itchy throat, and I don’t really have heartburn or reflux. I haven’t had fevers or night sweats, and I do have the weight loss of about 4.6 kg without trying, but no numbness/tingling—just progressive weakness and some leg discomfort.

Doctor: Given the 3-month dry cough with significant unintentional weight loss and long smoking history, plus leg weakness that improves with warming, I’m concerned about either lung malignancy with systemic effects or a paraneoplastic syndrome—can you tell me if you have new shortness of breath at rest, hoarseness, or swollen lymph nodes, and whether the weakness is symmetric or one-sided? Doctor: Also, on exam we need to check for muscle strength/reflex changes and signs of myopathy—are you able to rise from a chair or climb without hand support, and do you have any back pain? Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray, REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential, REQUEST TEST: CMP, REQUEST TEST: Sputum_cytology_if_producing (even if dry), REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast

RESULTS: Temperature 37.0°C (98.6°F); Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg; Heart Rate 72 bpm; Respiratory Rate 18 breaths/min. Pupillary response: equal, sluggishly reactive to light. Muscle strength: proximal lower extremity initially 3/5, improving to 5/5 upon repeated muscle tapping. Deep tendon reflexes: Achilles reflex 1+. Mucous membranes: dry. Serum electrolytes: Na 140 mEq/L, K 4.3 mEq/L, Cl 104 mEq/L, Ca 9.2 mg/dL. CBC: WBC 7,800 /μL, Hemoglobin 14.2 g/dL, Platelets 230,000 /μL. PFTs: normal spirometry. Voltage-gated calcium channel antibody: elevated.

Doctor: The elevated voltage-gated calcium channel antibody plus the proximal “stiff/weak” leg pattern that improves with repeated use (and largely normal CBC/PFTs) makes me think of Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome (often paraneoplastic), likely from a small-cell lung cancer—do you have any new shortness of breath, chest discomfort, hoarseness, or a history of smoking-related malignancy, and have you had any abnormal imaging yet? Doctor: On exam I’d expect fatigability with improving strength after brief exercise and reduced reflexes (your Achilles 1+ fits); if CT chest hasn’t been done, I need it immediately to look for small-cell lung cancer. Doctor: REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_with_contrast; REQUEST TEST: Serum_creatine_kinase_and_Magnesium; REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain_or_Cervical_spine_if_neuro_symptoms; DIAGNOSIS READY: Lambert–Eaton myasthenic syndrome (paraneoplastic), likely secondary to small-cell lung carcinoma
